sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, talk about the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新一期节目，当然，我们要聊的是关于我们20多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about birthday anxiety today because it is my birthday.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊聊生日焦虑，因为今天是我的生日。

sentences.en: The day that this comes out, I am turning 25, 25 years old.
sentences.zh: 在这一集发布的时候，我25岁了，25岁了。

sentences.en: We are halfway through the psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 我们已经走过了《20多岁心理学》的一半路程。

sentences.en: And the biggest question I always get is whether I'm going to do a psychology of your 30s.
sentences.zh: 我被问到最多的一个问题就是，我是否会做《30多岁心理学》。

sentences.en: I have five more years to think about it.
sentences.zh: 我还有五年时间来考虑这个问题。

sentences.en: So I will answer that question a little bit closer to the date.
sentences.zh: 所以，我会等到临近那个日期时再回答这个问题。

sentences.en: But yeah, it's my birthday and it's bringing up a lot of feelings, but it's also probably the most peaceful, serene birthday I have had.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，今天是我的生日，这勾起了我很多感受，但这可能也是我度过的最平静、最安详的一个生日。

sentences.en: I have never felt more comfortable with aging and more comfortable with the age that I'm at and more comfortable with what I'm choosing to do today than ever before.
sentences.zh: 我从未像现在这样对变老感到如此自在，对现在的年龄感到如此舒适，对今天所做的选择感到如此坦然。

sentences.en: And it's made me really, really reflective and it's made me want to talk about this experience of birthday anxiety that I've had for so long
sentences.zh: 这让我进行了非常深刻的反思，也让我想要谈谈这种我长期以来经历的生日焦虑，

sentences.en: and all the stress that usually comes with gaining another year, gaining another year of life, gaining another year of experiences.
sentences.zh: 以及通常伴随着又长一岁、又多了一年生命、又多了一年经历而来的所有压力。

sentences.en: And I want you to note that I did not say getting older.
sentences.zh: 我想请你注意，我没有说“变老”。

sentences.en: I like to position it as something that we are given, something that we are gifted.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把它定位为我们被赋予的东西，一种馈赠。

sentences.en: So this year I'm in New York City.
sentences.zh: 所以今年我在纽约市。

sentences.en: I've been in the US for like two and a half weeks for work, for work being this podcast and for mantra, of course, doing some like amazing recordings
sentences.zh: 我来美国大约两周半了，是为了工作，工作就是指这个播客，当然还有Mantra，进行了一些很棒的录音，

sentences.en: with some incredible guests that are coming out soon.
sentences.zh: 邀请了一些即将登场的不可思议的嘉宾。

sentences.en: And by being in New York, I know a few people, but honestly, like I don't have a huge, broad, wide group of friends here.
sentences.zh: 虽然在纽约，我认识几个人，但老实说，我在这里并没有一个庞大、广泛的朋友圈。

sentences.en: My boyfriend's back in Australia or my close friends, my family are back in Australia.
sentences.zh: 我的男朋友在澳大利亚，我的密友和家人也都在澳大利亚。

sentences.en: So I couldn't do like a big thing this year.
sentences.zh: 所以我今年没法搞什么大阵仗。

sentences.en: I couldn't do like a big party.
sentences.zh: 我没法办什么大型派对。

sentences.en: I couldn't like celebrate with my closest loved ones.
sentences.zh: 我没法和最亲近的爱人们一起庆祝。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I think that's part of why I feel so serene about it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这就是我感到如此平静的部分原因。

sentences.en: Like my plan is to go to a diner tonight and I'm going to get breakfast for dinner and I'm going to do my little birthday routine, which I'll talk about later in the episode
sentences.zh: 我的计划是今晚去一家餐馆，我要吃一份晚餐早餐，然后进行我那套小小的生日仪式，我会在节目后面讲到，

sentences.en: that I do every single year.
sentences.zh: 这是我每年都会做的。

sentences.en: And I have never felt more excited about it.
sentences.zh: 我从未对此感到如此兴奋。

sentences.en: Like I said before, this experience has not always been the case.
sentences.zh: 就像我之前说的，这种体验并不总是这样。

sentences.en: And I am sure for many of you who are listening, you don't find that this is the common theme that defines your birthday.
sentences.zh: 我相信对于许多正在收听的你们来说，你们并不觉得这是定义你们生日的主旋律。

sentences.en: It's normally quite an intense experience.
sentences.zh: 这通常是一种相当强烈的体验。

sentences.en: Birthdays are really, really reflective by nature.
sentences.zh: 生日本质上是非常引人反思的。

sentences.en: You know, they demand pause much like a new year.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们要求你停下来，就像新年一样。

sentences.en: You know, they feel like this very specific point in time where everything from the past feels very present and you're ruminating on who you are, what you've learned,
sentences.zh: 它们感觉像是时间轴上一个非常特殊的点，过去的一切都显得历历在目，你会在脑海中反复咀嚼你是谁、你学到了什么，

sentences.en: and also who you want to become.
sentences.zh: 以及你想成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: Like you're very focused on the future.
sentences.zh: 你非常关注未来。

sentences.en: We're getting older.
sentences.zh: 我们正在变老。

sentences.en: What if things don't work out the way I want?
sentences.zh: 如果事情没有按照我想要的方式发展怎么办？

sentences.en: I have less time.
sentences.zh: 我的时间变少了。

sentences.en: I feel like my body is aging, even though if you're in your 20s, like you're still really at the peak of your youth.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的身体在衰老，尽管如果你在20多岁，你其实正处于青春的巅峰。

sentences.en: But all of these feelings and this contemplation is naturally very paralyzing.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些感受和沉思自然是非常令人瘫痪的。

sentences.en: And that combined with a very sensitive social element as well.
sentences.zh: 再加上一个非常敏感的社交因素。

sentences.en: You know, the pressure to be around friends, the pressure to do a big thing, the pressure to have fun, all of that can create a real cocktail of complicated emotions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，周围人的压力、搞大排场的压力、必须玩得开心的压力，所有这些都会产生一种复杂的混合情绪。

sentences.en: And surprise, surprise, a lot about this does come down to our psychology as humans, as very deep thinking creatures and creatures who nonetheless love celebrations,
sentences.zh: 惊喜惊喜，这很大程度上归结于我们作为人类的心理，作为深思熟虑的生物，同时也是热爱庆祝活动的生物，

sentences.en: but also feel overwhelmed by them at times.
sentences.zh: 但有时也会被它们压得喘不过气来。

sentences.en: You know, we're full of oxymorons and contradictions, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 看来我们充满了矛盾和反差。

sentences.en: But today we are going to hopefully all together feel a little bit better about birthdays.
sentences.zh: 但今天，希望我们能一起对生日感觉好一点。

sentences.en: I want to talk about what makes them so difficult at times, specifically the three main reasons that we struggle with gaining another year.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈是什么让生日有时变得如此困难，特别是我们为又长一岁而挣扎的三个主要原因。

sentences.en: And then I also want to talk about why and how to rethink this process of aging and to rethink birthdays in general so that they are something that you look forward to,
sentences.zh: 然后我还想谈谈为什么要以及如何重新思考这个衰老的过程，重新思考生日，这样它们就会成为你所期待的，

sentences.en: that you're excited about, that is not stressful, and that if anything can actually bring you a lot of knowledge about yourself
sentences.zh: 让你感到兴奋的，没有压力的，如果有什么的话，它们实际上可以带给你很多关于你自己的知识，

sentences.en: and a really important space to reflect and grow into this next year of who you're becoming and who you're going to be.
sentences.zh: 并提供一个非常重要的空间来反思和成长，迎接你即将成为的下一个年度的自己。

sentences.en: So I know birthdays in our 20s are a big topic and so many of you have asked me for this.
sentences.zh: 我知道20多岁的生日是一个大话题，你们很多人都问过我这个问题。

sentences.en: So I'm going to stop rambling.
sentences.zh: 所以我要停止唠叨了。

sentences.en: And without further ado, let's talk about the psychology of birthday anxiety.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们来谈谈生日焦虑的心理学。

sentences.en: So I think the reason that birthdays can be so psychologically, mentally, emotionally, sometimes socially taxing comes down to three specific reasons.
sentences.zh: 我认为生日之所以在心理、精神、情感甚至社交上让人感到负担，归结为三个具体原因。

sentences.en: The first is very existential reasons to do with aging, to do with progress, to do with milestones.
sentences.zh: 第一是与衰老、进步、里程碑有关的非常存在主义的原因。

sentences.en: The second comes down to expectations and the pressure to seemingly have this perfect event or this perfect experience to mark another year.
sentences.zh: 第二归结于期望，以及为了纪念又一年而必须拥有完美活动或完美体验的压力。

sentences.en: And the third series of reasons, I think, are quite social reasons that have to do with loneliness, perhaps a great deal of comparison as well.
sentences.zh: 第三系列原因，我认为是相当社交性的，与孤独有关，或许还有大量的比较。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about each of these individually, starting with very existential reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以我想逐一谈谈这些，从非常存在主义的原因开始。

sentences.en: So I think for the longest time, the reason birthdays felt so troublesome to me was that it was a sign that I was getting older.
sentences.zh: 我认为很长一段时间以来，生日让我感到困扰的原因是，它标志着我在变老。

sentences.en: And that is something that was very, very scary.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常、非常可怕的事情。

sentences.en: My perspective on aging, though, has changed.
sentences.zh: 不过，我对衰老的看法已经改变了。

sentences.en: And I used to be really scared of it.
sentences.zh: 我曾经非常害怕它。

sentences.en: I used to joke with my friends that I would be forever 22.
sentences.zh: 我过去常和朋友开玩笑说，我会永远22岁。

sentences.en: The reason that we are scared of aging, and if you can relate to this,
sentences.zh: 我们害怕衰老的原因，如果你能感同身受，

sentences.en: I'm sure you've already come to this conclusion.
sentences.zh: 我相信你已经得出了这个结论。

sentences.en: The reason that we are scared of aging is because we are scared of the unknown.
sentences.zh: 我们害怕衰老是因为我们害怕未知。

sentences.en: We are naturally, as humans, always going to feel a little bit anxious and a little bit uncomfortable with somewhere and some place that we have never been before.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们天生就会对从未去过的地方和境地感到焦虑和不安。

sentences.en: You have never been in this next year of your life.
sentences.zh: 你从未经历过你生命中的下一年。

sentences.en: You have never been 27.
sentences.zh: 你从未27岁过。

sentences.en: You have never been 35.
sentences.zh: 你从未35岁过。

sentences.en: You have never been 66.
sentences.zh: 你从未66岁过。

sentences.en: And so because of that, it feels very unknown, very uncertain, very unstable.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，它感觉非常未知、非常不确定、非常不稳定。

sentences.en: And with that empty space and with that uncertainty, our brain likes to fill that with fear.
sentences.zh: 面对那片空白和不确定性，我们的大脑喜欢用恐惧来填补它。

sentences.en: It likes to fill that with catastrophic ideas and imaginations of what it's going to be like.
sentences.zh: 它喜欢用灾难性的想法和对未来的想象来填补它。

sentences.en: And they're not always positive.
sentences.zh: 而且这些想法并不总是积极的。

sentences.en: The other reason that we are scared of aging, other than the fear of the unknown, is a similar fear of the unknown.
sentences.zh: 我们害怕衰老的另一个原因，除了对未知的恐惧之外，是一种类似的对未知的恐惧。

sentences.en: And it's a fear of death.
sentences.zh: 那就是对死亡的恐惧。

sentences.en: It feels like each year we are, you know, closer to the end of this journey than the beginning.
sentences.zh: 感觉每过一年，我们离这段旅程的终点就比起点更近了。

sentences.en: I used to be very, very scared of this.
sentences.zh: 我曾经非常、非常害怕这一点。

sentences.en: And I can openly admit that and talk about it now because of how much time I have spent thinking about it and overthinking it and intellectualizing it till the cows came in.
sentences.zh: 我现在可以公开承认并谈论它，因为我花了很多时间去思考、过度思考，并把它理性化到了极致。

sentences.en: Like, it was an obsessive thought of me, for me for so long of what happens after we die.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说曾是一个长期的强迫性念头：我们死后会发生什么？

sentences.en: And aging is just this terrible thing that's bringing me closer.
sentences.zh: 而衰老只是那件让我离终点更近的可怕事情。

sentences.en: Then I realized that aging is actually absolutely necessary because the alternative to not getting older is that you would always stay the same
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到，衰老实际上是绝对必要的，因为不衰老的替代方案就是你永远保持不变，

sentences.en: and that you would always stay in the same place as the same past version of you.
sentences.zh: 你永远停留在同一个地方，作为过去版本的自己。

sentences.en: You would never be able to grow and you would never be able to experience new chapters.
sentences.zh: 你永远无法成长，也永远无法体验新的篇章。

sentences.en: Turning 25, 27, 28.
Yes, it's a privilege and I know a lot of people talk about how there are so many people who don't make it to that age and you should live for them
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种特权，我知道很多人谈论有多少人没能活到那个年纪，你应该为他们而活，

sentences.en: and realize that it's an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 并意识到这是一个机会。

sentences.en: Yes, that's one way of seeing it but I also think that time holds experiences.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种看待方式，但我还认为时间承载着经历。

sentences.en: And so, if this world was perfectly designed or however you want to think about it, aging is an important part of that because aging is what brings you into the future.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这个世界是完美设计的，或者无论你怎么想，衰老都是其中重要的一部分，因为衰老带你走向未来。

sentences.en: Aging is what brings you excitement, brings you surprises.
sentences.zh: 衰老带给你兴奋，带给你惊喜。

sentences.en: If you were to stay 17 for your whole life, if you were to stay 25 for your whole life, you would never get to experience what it's like to be a grandparent,
sentences.zh: 如果你一生都保持17岁，如果你一生都保持25岁，你就永远无法体验成为祖父母的感觉，

sentences.en: what it's like to be senior in your career, what it's like to own a home that you love, what it's like to gain maturity and perspective,
sentences.zh: 无法体验在职业生涯中成为资深人士的感觉，无法体验拥有一套你热爱的房子的感觉，无法体验获得成熟和视角的感觉，

sentences.en: what it's like to feel your frontal lobe develop.
sentences.zh: 无法体验感受你的额叶发育的感觉。

sentences.en: That is really how I started to see it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我开始看待它的方式。

sentences.en: Another way I started to see it in my brain that felt more comfortable is that age is really just a number and it's so cliche, I know, but it is so true.
sentences.zh: 我在大脑中开始看待它的另一种方式，让我感觉更舒服，那就是年龄真的只是一个数字，我知道这很陈词滥调，但它确实如此。

sentences.en: It is so true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I see this philosophy reflected in so many people that I love and that I know in my life.
sentences.zh: 我在我所爱的人和生活中认识的人身上看到了这种哲学。

sentences.en: So, a couple weeks ago, I celebrated my grandfather's 90th birthday.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我庆祝了我祖父的90岁生日。

sentences.en: Now, that man turned 90, he drank more than me.
sentences.zh: 那个男人90岁了，他喝得比我还多。

sentences.en: He drank more than any 21-year-old.
sentences.zh: 他喝得比任何21岁的人都多。

sentences.en: He pulled out like this really nice bottle of port.
sentences.zh: 他拿出了这瓶非常好的波特酒。

sentences.en: He had this big birthday cake, all of his friends.
sentences.zh: 他有一个大生日蛋糕，所有的朋友都来了。

sentences.en: My sisters, who are literally like 18 and I don't know, 17 at this point, genuinely, like they left before the night was even over.
sentences.zh: 我的姐妹们，她们才18岁和17岁，老实说，她们在夜晚结束前就离开了。

sentences.en: Like, my grandparents were the last to go.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父母是最后走的。

sentences.en: We walked home with them, all tipsy and drunk and not only was my grandfather still this, like, had this youthful exuberance and really wasn't showing his age,
sentences.zh: 我们和他们一起走回家，大家都醉醺醺的，不仅我祖父依然保持着这种青春活力，一点也不显老，

sentences.en: but he also had, you know, the blessing of so many stories that we got to hear.
sentences.zh: 而且他还拥有我们有幸听到的许多故事的祝福。

sentences.en: And it made me realize, like, you can take your age as a sign of who you need to be and you need to be this person who becomes more grouchy.
sentences.zh: 这让我意识到，你可以把年龄当作你需要成为什么样的人的标志，你需要成为那个变得越来越暴躁的人，

sentences.en: You need to be this person who, according to society, becomes less happy and exudes less joy and finds less pleasure in things.
sentences.zh: 你需要成为那个按照社会标准，变得不那么快乐、散发更少喜悦、从事物中发现更少乐趣的人。

sentences.en: But you also have the choice to take your age,
sentences.zh: 但你也可以选择如何看待你的年龄，

sentences.en: you know, keep it as something that's just on your birth certificate or just on your driver's license and embody the ages that you feel and all the positive parts of that age
sentences.zh: 你知道，把它仅仅当作出生证明或驾照上的一个数字，去体现你内心感受到的年龄，以及那个年龄段中所有你想要保留的积极部分，

sentences.en: that you want to bring forward with you.
sentences.zh: 并带着它们继续前行。

sentences.en: Another reason that birthdays can bring up some negative feelings and some specifically existential feelings comes down to feeling behind when it comes to your life plans.
sentences.zh: 生日之所以会带来一些负面情绪，尤其是某种存在主义式的焦虑，另一个原因在于当你审视自己的人生规划时，会感到自己落后了。

sentences.en: Feeling like you should be further ahead, feeling like you should be more accomplished and yet here you are and you look around, everyone else seems to be doing
sentences.zh: 感觉自己本该走得更远，感觉自己本该取得更多成就，但看看周围，其他人似乎都在做着

sentences.en: these amazing things and you're lost and you're behind.
sentences.zh: 那些了不起的事情，而你却感到迷茫，感到自己落后了。

sentences.en: And now as you get older, all it's going to be is this game of catch up.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，这一切只会变成一场永无止境的追赶游戏。

sentences.en: If you can relate to that, I think what you're experiencing is not so much birthday anxiety, but milestone anxiety.
sentences.zh: 如果你对此感同身受，我想你经历的与其说是生日焦虑，不如说是里程碑焦虑。

sentences.en: Anxiety to do with feeling like you are not hitting specific
sentences.zh: 这种焦虑源于你觉得自己在该达成的时候，

sentences.en: socially approved targets when you should be.
sentences.zh: 没有达到那些社会公认的目标。

sentences.en: Now, this is a real conundrum for a lot of us in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我们许多二十多岁的人面临的一个难题。

sentences.en: I saw this quote the other day that it feels like between the ages of 18 and 35, we're all in some imaginary race and we're not sure what the race is,
sentences.zh: 前几天我看到一句话，大意是说在18到35岁之间，我们仿佛都置身于一场虚构的竞赛中，虽然我们并不确定这场竞赛比的是什么，

sentences.en: but we know that we're behind.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道自己落后了。

sentences.en: That is really what this period in our life feels like.
sentences.zh: 这确实就是我们人生这一阶段的真实写照。

sentences.en: And a lot of it does come down to comparison against our peers, but also comparison against this weird indoctrinated blueprint that we all seem to understand.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上，这归结于与同龄人的比较，也归结于我们似乎都认同的那种奇怪的、被灌输的人生蓝图。

sentences.en: We all seem to have this weird sense that by 30, you know, we probably should have should be married by 25.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎都有种奇怪的观念，觉得到了30岁，你知道，我们可能应该在25岁时就结婚了。

sentences.en: We should be knowing what we want to do with our career by 28.
sentences.zh: 我们应该在28岁时就知道自己的职业规划。

sentences.en: We should have met our best friends.
sentences.zh: 我们应该已经遇到了最好的朋友。

sentences.en: We should have bought a home.
sentences.zh: 我们应该已经买了房。

sentences.en: There are all these like seemingly important milestones to hit before you reach your 30s.
sentences.zh: 在步入30岁之前，似乎有这么多看似重要的里程碑需要达成。

sentences.en: And the thing is all of those milestones are external.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，所有这些里程碑都是外在的。

sentences.en: We do not compare important measures like happiness.
sentences.zh: 我们不会去比较幸福感这样重要的衡量标准。

sentences.en: We do not compare important things like growth, like self-knowledge, authenticity.
sentences.zh: 我们不会去比较成长、自我认知、真实性这些重要的东西。

sentences.en: We don't think about how far how far advanced we are in terms of our emotions and how we internally feel.
sentences.zh: 我们不会去思考自己在情感和内心感受方面进步了多少。

sentences.en: We are really focused on the external, how our life appears to other people and that is a huge source of disappointment and sadness and frustration.
sentences.zh: 我们太过于关注外在，关注我们的生活在别人眼中是什么样子，而这正是失望、悲伤和挫败感的巨大来源。

sentences.en: Birthdays, I think, just really naturally bring that out.
sentences.zh: 我认为，生日自然而然地把这些情绪激发了出来。

sentences.en: I will also say we also are very, very focused to our fault at comparing ourselves to people who are doing better than us.
sentences.zh: 我还想说，我们也非常、非常习惯于——甚至到了自讨苦吃的地步——去和那些比我们过得好的人比较。

sentences.en: We often engage in what we call upward social comparison, knowing that it's going to make us feel bad, knowing that it's going to hurt our self-concept and our self-esteem,
sentences.zh: 我们经常进行所谓的“向上社会比较”，明知这会让自己感觉糟糕，明知这会伤害我们的自我认知和自尊，

sentences.en: but we just can't help ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但我们就是无法克制。

sentences.en: It's like we almost convince ourselves subconsciously, mentally, that if I feel bad enough about where I am, maybe that will force me to work harder.
sentences.zh: 就好像我们在潜意识里说服自己，如果我对现状感到足够糟糕，也许就能强迫自己更加努力。

sentences.en: If I look at someone that I'm envious of or that makes me feel less accomplished, maybe that's this weird sense of self-punishment that's going to motivate me
sentences.zh: 如果我盯着那些让我嫉妒的人，或者那些让我觉得自己成就不足的人，也许这是一种奇怪的自我惩罚，能激励我，

sentences.en: and that is absolutely not the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实绝非如此。

sentences.en: There is no big finish line that we are all working towards.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人并不是在奔向同一个终点线。

sentences.en: Like not one single person on this planet has the exact same goals and the exact same vision of what their life looks like.
sentences.zh: 这个星球上没有哪两个人拥有完全相同的目标，也没有人对生活有着完全相同的愿景。

sentences.en: It's all different and even people who get to the point or even people who you admire for getting to the point that you want to be, they are still looking at their life and feeling
sentences.zh: 每个人的情况都不同，即使是那些达到了你所向往的成就、让你羡慕的人，他们也在审视自己的生活，并感到

sentences.en: some sense of dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 某种程度的不满足。

sentences.en: I can absolutely tell you that.
sentences.zh: 我可以非常肯定地告诉你这一点。

sentences.en: It may even be the case that they are looking at you and thinking,
sentences.zh: 甚至可能他们正在看着你，心想：

sentences.en: God, I really wish I had as much peace as this person has.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我真希望自己能像这个人一样内心平静。

sentences.en: I really wish I had as much time and space for growth.
sentences.zh: 我真希望自己能有这么多时间和空间去成长。

sentences.en: I really wish that I was still at the beginning so I could make different choices.
sentences.zh: 我真希望自己还处于起步阶段，这样我就能做出不同的选择。

sentences.en: There is something to be compared against or with for every single person.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有可以与之比较的对象。

sentences.en: So as you're comparing yourself to someone else, they're comparing themselves to someone else who's probably comparing themselves to you.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你拿自己和别人比较时，他们也在拿自己和别人比较，而那个人可能也在拿自己和你比较。

sentences.en: So I know that can be a really, really hard part about birthdays is feeling behind and feeling lost in your 20s.
sentences.zh: 我知道，在二十多岁时感到落后和迷茫，这确实是生日中最难熬的一部分。

sentences.en: I always remind myself when I'm at that point because I think as humans we all end up in that comparison spiral.
sentences.zh: 每当我处于那种状态时，我总会提醒自己——因为我觉得作为人类，我们最终都会陷入那种比较的漩涡——

sentences.en: I always remind myself to think about what I've achieved in terms of personal growth and reflection in the last year.
sentences.zh: 我总是提醒自己去思考过去一年里我在个人成长和反思方面取得了什么成就。

sentences.en: So as I'm turning 25, I feel like this 24th year of my life, I became so much better at feeling less pressure around social media,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我快25岁时，我觉得在24岁这一年里，我变得更擅长减少社交媒体带来的压力，

sentences.en: I became so much better in managing my overthinking, I became so much better in feeling satisfied with the friends that I have rather than feeling like I constantly needed more
sentences.zh: 我变得更擅长管理自己的过度思考，我变得更擅长对自己拥有的朋友感到满足，而不是总觉得还需要更多，

sentences.en: or that I was constantly on the precipice of loneliness.
sentences.zh: 或者总觉得自己处于孤独的边缘。

sentences.en: That means more to me and that impacts me positively more on the daily than any kind of achievement that I've had publicly.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说意义更重大，它每天对我的积极影响，远胜于我取得的任何公开成就。

sentences.en: That sense of inner growth and homeostasis and progress is really, really important.
sentences.zh: 那种内心的成长、平衡和进步感真的非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: Okay, we are going to take a short break but when we return I want to talk about two of the final reasons that we feel a lot of stress, anxiety, maybe sadness around our birthdays
sentences.zh: 好了，我们要休息一下，但回来后我想谈谈我们对生日感到压力、焦虑甚至悲伤的最后两个原因，

sentences.en: and my perfect routine for combating that.
sentences.zh: 以及我应对这种情绪的完美方案。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the second reason that birthdays can be so hard and it's expectations.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈生日难熬的第二个原因，那就是期望。

sentences.en: It's this pressure to have this perfect, perfect day.
sentences.zh: 这是一种想要度过完美一天的压力，

sentences.en: this perfect party, these perfect friends who are all going to wish us happy birthday
sentences.zh: 完美的派对，完美的朋友，他们都会祝我们生日快乐，

sentences.en: and often we are let down.
sentences.zh: 而我们往往会感到失望。

sentences.en: I would say
sentences.zh: 我想说，

sentences.en: 99% of the time when you have grand aspirations for a big birthday blowout and you know how you expect everyone to treat you, you're often disappointed.
sentences.zh: 99%的情况下，当你对盛大的生日派对抱有宏大期望，并且期待每个人都以某种方式对待你时，你往往会感到失望。

sentences.en: I think anytime we say that we are supposed to do something, we're supposed to be happy, we're supposed to be loved, we're supposed to have all this fun, we're supposed
sentences.zh: 我认为，每当我们说我们“应该”做什么，我们“应该”快乐，我们“应该”被爱，我们“应该”玩得开心，我们“应该”

sentences.en: to just ease through this, you are setting yourself up for disappointment.
sentences.zh: 轻松度过这一天时，你就是在为自己的失望做铺垫。

sentences.en: When we put should or supposed to before anything, often it's not going to look the way that we have imagined it.
sentences.zh: 当我们给任何事情加上“应该”这个词时，它往往不会呈现出我们想象中的样子。

sentences.en: Now I think this also comes down to comparison, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这同样归结于比较，对吧？

sentences.en: We see people having these huge birthdays with lots and lots of friends and it looks so fun and they look celebrated and loved.
sentences.zh: 我们看到别人举办盛大的生日派对，有很多很多朋友，看起来非常开心，他们看起来被庆祝、被爱着。

sentences.en: Of course we want that, that looks amazing.
sentences.zh: 我们当然想要那样，那看起来太棒了。

sentences.en: And so we go about trying to make that happen.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始尝试去实现它。

sentences.en: The thing that we don't see in those photos, in those pictures is all the stress that usually comes with having those kinds of huge events and huge expectations.
sentences.zh: 但我们在那些照片里看不到的，是举办这类大型活动和抱有巨大期望通常伴随而来的所有压力。

sentences.en: Now if you are someone who specifically struggles with control, the idea of like a big birthday party that might seem really impressive and fun from the outside is probably
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个特别纠结于掌控感的人，那么从外表看可能非常令人印象深刻且有趣的盛大生日派对，很可能

sentences.en: going to cause you a lot of internal chaos.
sentences.zh: 会让你内心陷入混乱。

sentences.en: For the starters, you're going to want every single thing to go perfectly, you're going to want it to perhaps look exactly as you imagined it and you are going to feel responsible
sentences.zh: 首先，你会希望每一件事都完美无缺，你可能希望它看起来和你想象中一模一样，而且你会觉得有责任

sentences.en: for other people's fun.
sentences.zh: 去确保别人玩得开心。

sentences.en: Tell me if you relate to this but I have often found whenever I have thrown big birthday parties,
sentences.zh: 告诉我你是否有同感，但我经常发现，每当我举办大型生日派对时，

sentences.en: I always spend about
sentences.zh: 我总是花大约

sentences.en: 50% of the night looking around me and making sure that people are chatting, making sure that people are enjoying themselves.
sentences.zh: 50%的时间环顾四周，确保人们在聊天，确保人们玩得尽兴。

sentences.en: I most certainly spend the first hour wondering if people are going to show up, wondering if people are going to go away and say that was fun or they're going to leave early.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会花第一个小时担心人们会不会来，担心人们走的时候会不会说“真好玩”，或者他们会不会提前离开。

sentences.en: Now, for a day that should be focused on you and should be focused on this incredible achievement of growing up and experiencing more, I find that big events like that take all of
sentences.zh: 对于一个本该以你为中心，本该庆祝你成长和经历更多精彩成就的日子，我发现这种大型活动会把

sentences.en: the attention you should be showing yourself off of you and on to managing other people's feelings and other people's perceptions.
sentences.zh: 本该关注自己的注意力，转移到去管理别人的感受和看法上。

sentences.en: It often creates this experience where you can only feel happy in hindsight.
sentences.zh: 这往往会导致一种只有在事后回想时才能感到快乐的体验。

sentences.en: You can only feel happy with rose tinted glasses on.
sentences.zh: 只有戴上玫瑰色的滤镜，你才能感到快乐。

sentences.en: So, throughout the day you've probably felt very on edge, very overwhelmed, very rushed.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这一整天里，你可能一直感到如坐针毡、不知所措、匆匆忙忙。

sentences.en: Then during the event maybe you get like a couple of hours of a bit of bliss but you're still worried about other people's feelings and then the next morning sometimes you
sentences.zh: 然后在活动期间，也许你能享受几个小时的片刻欢愉，但你仍然在担心别人的感受，第二天早上有时甚至

sentences.en: even have like a bit of an emotional and social
sentences.zh: 会有一种情感和社交上的

sentences.en: hangover and then it still may not have met your expectations and you've put money into this party and you've put your hopes and dreams into it.
sentences.zh: “宿醉”，而且它可能还没达到你的期望，你为这个派对投入了金钱，投入了希望和梦想。

sentences.en: That can lead us to feel very very let down.
sentences.zh: 这会导致我们感到非常、非常失望。

sentences.en: You may also have the experience of not telling people what you want, not wanting to be a burden, not wanting to like outwardly say hey please make a big deal about me, please make
sentences.zh: 你可能还会经历那种不告诉别人你想要什么的情况，不想成为负担，不想表现得好像在说“嘿，请为我大张旗鼓地庆祝”，

sentences.en: a fuss and because you haven't communicated it everyone thinks you want some small thing
sentences.zh: 因为你没有沟通清楚，每个人都以为你只想要点小庆祝，

sentences.en: you're left disappointed because you wish that someone had read your mind and the sad thing is that they couldn't and you know it's like you can't go out and say like I want a
sentences.zh: 结果你感到失望，因为你希望有人能读懂你的心思。可悲的是，他们做不到。你知道，你不能直接说“我想要一个

sentences.en: surprise birthday party because then you're not surprised but some part of you is like I just wish these people would be able to see into my brain and know what I want which
sentences.zh: 惊喜生日派对”，因为那样就不是惊喜了。但你内心深处会想：我真希望这些人能看穿我的大脑，知道我想要什么。而这，

sentences.en: even for our closest most nearest and dearest friends is sometimes impossible.
sentences.zh: 即使是对我们最亲近、最亲密的朋友来说，有时也是不可能的。

sentences.en: On the flip side I've also spoken to people who have said to me I have these big expectations
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我也和一些人聊过，他们对我说：“我有这些巨大的期望，

sentences.en: but I also know that I'm going to feel very awkward being the center of attention and I know I'm going to feel very strange about it because I have this fear of being perceived
sentences.zh: 但我同时也知道，成为关注焦点会让我感到非常尴尬，我知道我会对此感到非常奇怪，因为我害怕被审视，

sentences.en: but I can't help that feel like that if I don't do this I'm also going to be very lonely and
sentences.zh: 但我又忍不住觉得，如果我不这样做，我会感到非常孤独，
